newsitem.title: INDONESIA: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - June 24.
newsitem.headline: INDONESIAN STOCKS - factors to watch - June 24.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors likely to affect Indonesian stocks on Tuesday:

* U.S. stocks ended sharply lower on Monday after comments from Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto about the potential sale of U.S. government securities by Japan triggered a wave of profit-taking. The Dow industrials finished down 192 points, or 2.5 percent, at 7604.

* Indonesia's three authorised political parties on Monday formally accepted the results of May 29 general elections, but one party expressed concern about alleged poll violations and the conduct of the campaign.

* On Monday, Jakarta's composite index ended at a record closing high on active local buying of secondaries and modest interest in blue-chips. The index closed 1.04 percent, or 7.41 points, higher at 719.64 points after touching a intra-day high of 719.79 points only minutes earlier.
* On Tuesday, the rupiah was quoted at 2,430.00/32.00 at 0105 GMT, compared with an opening of 2,429.50/30.50.

* Bakrie Land Development after its holding company PT Bakrie Capital Indonesia announced that it planned to buy 11,250,000 shares of another property company PT Bumi Modern at a price of 2,475 rupiah per share through a tender offer. PT Bakrie Capital Indonesia owns 70 percent of Bakrie Land Development, a property firm which used to be known as PT Elang Realty.

* Medium-sized property firm PT Panca Wiratama Sakti after privately-owned property company PT Intermustika Mutiara announced that it planned to buy 16,830 million shares or a 51 percent stake in Panca Wiratama at 1,750 rupiah per share through a tender.

* Pulp and paper maker Indah Kiat Pulp and Paper after it won shareholder approval for a 45-for-50 rights issue, attached with 14 warrants. The proceeds were estimated at 2.5 trillion rupiah from the rights and 471 billion rupiah from the warrant. The company has said the funds will be used to purchase three paper processing machines.
* Noodle maker Indofood and its sister company Indocement ahead of their annual shareholder meetings in the afternoon.
* Retailer Matahari Putra Prima after it won shareholder approval to pay a 1996 dividend of 15 rupiah per share and split the nominal value of its stock.
* Bank Umum on the payment of 70.59 rupiah dividend per share for 1996.
* Timber firm PT Barito Pacific after it said on Monday that it will pay a 55 rupiah dividend for 1996.
* Texmaco Perkasa Engineering, PT Polysindo Eka Perkasa and Texmaco Jaya -- all under the Texmaco Group -- after shareholder approval to pay dividends of 90, 60 and 30 rupiah per share respectively.
* Medco Energy on media reports that it will propose a rights issue valued at 300 billion rupiah to finance an expansion programme.
